title: intent edit hands back a path at rc=0 for an Ac, At or Attachment that does not exist
body:
`intent edit` hands back a path at rc=0 for an Ac, an At or an Attachment
that does not exist. Found while fixing 0238, deliberately NOT fixed there,
and separated on vc's ruling so the unfixed part stays citable.

WHY IT IS NOT PART OF 0238. 0238 was a contained check: the entity door
already existed for the cases it covered. These three have no door to check
them with. `Facade` carries `st_show`, `wp_show` and `issue_show` and has NO
`ac_show`, no `at_show` and no attachment resolver, so closing this means
minting three model doors -- a build, not a check. Leaving it on 0238's body
would have made 0238 read FIXED while a third of its subject was not, and
every later citation of "0238, fixed" would inherit a claim that is only
partly true.

DRIVEN, `target/debug/intent` at 92e4d914a, throwaway estate under an
isolated HOME. ST0001 exists and has one real WP; nothing else named below
exists:

    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/ac/1 --path                rc=0
    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/at/1 --path                rc=0
    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/attachments/notes.md       rc=0

All three print `intent/st/ST0001/info.md` -- the THREAD's file. The
attachment case is the sharpest: `notes.md` was never created, and the tool
answers rc=0 with a path to a different file entirely.

THE ANSWER IS INVARIANT OVER THE ID, which is what makes this undetectable
by comparison. A real entity and an absent one print the same bytes, so no
golden file and no output diff can separate them. The only detectable form
is a refusal, which is why the fix must refuse before answering rather than
answer better. Same reasoning ratified on 0238.

HOW THESE ARE REACHED, because the obvious bound does not hold. `edit`
declares `kind` as `st|wp|issue` and `check_enum` enforces it, so the
`<kind> <id>` spelling cannot express any of the three. The `intent://`
address arm is a SECOND ARGUMENT GRAMMAR inside the same verb and bypasses
`check_enum` entirely. `edited()`'s own comment says so in as many words:
"this is a second argument grammar inside one verb". Anyone bounding this
surface by the enum -- as this reporter first did -- will conclude these
variants are unreachable. They are not.

WHY THE SHARED DOOR DOES NOT ALREADY CATCH THEM. `Facade::edit` checks the
entity via `Entity::artefact()`, which collapses SIX variants onto their
THREAD: `Wp`, `Ac`, `At`, `Attachment`, `AcCollection` and `WpCollection`.
0238 added the `Wp` arm. These three remain, each needing a resolver that
does not exist.

NOT DEFECTS, and named so nobody re-files them: the two COLLECTION variants
(`intent:///threads/<id>/wp` and `/ac`). The collection of a thread that
exists also exists, empty or not, so the `st_show` already on that path is
the right and complete check. vc concurs.

WHERE IT WAS FOUND: 0238, which covered the `wp` case at this same door
(79047e3d) and the browse case (5a3b22fd), and which does NOT cover this.
